title: Where text blocks stop being the right tool

questions.stem: Per this page, which need calls for a template engine such as Thymeleaf rather than a text block with formatted()?

options.text: Substituting a few values into a short, mostly fixed template
options.says: The page lists simple variable substitution in a small template as the case where a text block is enough.

options.text: Keeping the template free of any cost while the program runs
options.says: The page names zero runtime overhead as a benefit of text blocks, which are compiled to constants, not of template engines.

options.text: Showing parts of the output only under a condition, or once per item
options.says: The page says text blocks have no if/else or loops, and names conditional logic or loops as the reason to use a template engine.

questions.stem: Per this page, where should a template that has grown to hundreds of lines live?

options.text: In a resource file that the code reads when it needs it
options.says: The page's pitfall says a template of hundreds of lines belongs in an external file, read as a resource, instead of inline.

options.text: In one text block, since the compiler makes it one constant
options.says: The page lists embedding very large templates inline as a pitfall, even though a text block has no runtime cost.

options.text: In several text blocks, one per section, joined with +
options.says: The page's advice for a template this size is an external file; splitting it keeps the same hundreds of lines inline.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
